articleTitle: A Highly Efficient Wide Battery Voltage Range Dual Active Bridge-Based Single-stage Bidirectional EV Onboard Charger Without Low-Frequency Harmonics in the Charging Current
abstract: This paper introduces an on-board charger circuit capable of converting 1-phase AC to DC in a single stage. The circuit integrates a PWM 2-level voltage-sourced inverter (VSI) and a dual active bridge (DAB) converter into a unified single-stage structure with the help of a suitably crafted modulation strategy. Single-phase 1-stage topologies are known to suffer from significant double line-frequency ripple in the charging current. The proposed combined pulse-width and phase-shift modulation strategy achieves active power decoupling without any extra circuitry, eliminating the double line-frequency AC ripple in the battery charging current. This also enables the least RMS DAB current trajectory throughout the line cycle while facilitating Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) for enhanced efficiency. The paper begins by detailing the working principle of the proposed converter, followed by an analytical examination of the modulation strategy. Simulation results indicate a peak power-stage efficiency exceeding 98 % for a 3.6k W J-phase system operating within a battery voltage range of 300V-500V. Experimental validation at 500W demonstrates efficiency levels consistent with the predicted values.

articleTitle: EV Charging Infrastructure: Smooth Power Delivery Using Pulse Charging Methods for Swappable Charging Station
abstract: The batteries are the primary power source for electric vehicle applications. The operation of the batteries is dependent on their regular charging process, where the charging patterns influence both the efficiency and longevity of batteries. Therefore, there is a need for an optimal charging strategy, which aims to extend the cycle life of the batteries. Among all the existing charging methods the pulse charging method is beneficial, which helps in synchronizing chemical reactions with the charging process, stabilizing reactions, and improving efficiency. Hence, this paper proposes an optimum charging algorithm based on pulse charging, which includes the combination of constant current, pulse current (PC), and pulse and burp current (PBC) charging for the swappable charging station. The power flowing from the grid to the charger side is pulsating in nature during PC and PBC charging. Therefore, a charging algorithm is proposed in this paper to provide smooth power transfer during PC and PBC charging. Furthermore, to reduce grid dependency, renewable sources such as wind and solar power are incorporated along with the main grid to form a DC microgrid environment. This system is capable of supplying excess power from renewable sources to the grid. This paper incorporates analysis and results of the proposed charging algorithm and renewable energy based system.

articleTitle: A Simple Active Balancing Technique for 5-Level Flying Capacitor Converters with Reduced Sensing Requirements
abstract: Flying-capacitor multi-level converters invariably require the flying-capacitor voltages to be balanced for optimal operation. Balancing is typically carried out using dedicated controllers that require multiple voltages to be sensed and operate multiple loops in parallel. This paper presents a simple control technique for flying-capacitor 5-level converters in which only one flying-capacitor voltage needs to be sensed, leading to reduced system, design, and hardware complexity. The technique, based on eliminating the main unbalancing mode of the converter using a single balancing loop, is theoretically developed through both steady-state and dynamic considerations, and validated in simulations as well as experimentally on a 12 V - 2.4 V, 200 kHz flying-capacitor 5-level converter prototype.

articleTitle: Non-isolated Single Inductor-Based Dual-Input Bidirectional DC-DC Converter with ZCS for Integrating Battery Stack
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-isolated dual-input single-output DC-DC converter. The proposed converter integrates two different battery stack using minimal components, along with a bidirectional power flow feature, facilitated by a single inductor. Furthermore, the converter structure enables semiconductor switches with Zero Current Switching (ZCS). The paper also discusses the operation of the proposed converter in two modes, and investigates the effect of parasitic elements on converter performance. A dynamic model of the proposed converter is developed, and stability analysis is presented. Finally, a laboratory prototype of the converter, rated at 200 W and 50 kHz, is successfully fabricated and tested.

articleTitle: High Power Density HV DCDC Converter for Aerospace
abstract: Achieving high efficiency and high-power density is a critical goal in many power electronics applications. LLC resonant converter has been proved as an excellent topology to achieve this goal. The growing popularity of the split resonant capacitor-based LLC resonant converter in its half-bridge configuration is due to its higher efficiency, higher power density and reliability. This configuration features the low level of EMI emissions too. Such features perfectly fit the power supply demand in the More Electric Aircraft (MEA). One of the major difficulties that engineers are facing with this topology is to understand the converter detail operation especially at the critical boundary conditions to operate in the soft switching mode and the design optimization. The purpose of this paper is to provide a detailed analytical approach of the steady state operation of the topology that we translated into a converter design procedure for aerospace power supply to achieve zero-voltage switching (ZVS) of primary switches and zero-current switching (ZCS) of secondary side in a wide input voltage range for Split capacitor based Half-bridge LLC resonant converters.

articleTitle: A Fault- Tolerant Multilevel Inverter Topology with Three Source Configuration Using Lower Number of Switches
abstract: For a reliable power electronic system, fault-tolerant power converters play an important role. Most of the power converter are highly prone to faults due to various operating conditions. A power quality assessment of a three-source topology has been carried out. Based on the analysis, a new fault-tolerant multilevel inverter (FT-MLI) has been proposed in this paper, which can be operated with switch open circuit fault conditions. The proposed FT -MLI has an additional three switches to achieve fault-tolerant operation. A fault-tolerant analysis along with the simulation and experimental results are provided to demonstrate the performance of the proposed FT-MLI topology.

articleTitle: Series Connected High Frequency Link Ripple Power Compensation Strategy for 1-phase Bidirectional Isolated AC- DC Matrix Converters
abstract: Addressing the compensation of double line frequency ripple power in the 1-ϕ operation of direct matrix converters is crucial for enhancing some of their key features such as power density, reliability, and cost-effectiveness. The available literature provides few solutions pertinent to matrix converter based high frequency isolated AC-DC topologies. Hence, this paper introduces a series connected active ripple power decoupling circuit that operates at the high frequency AC link of such matrix converter topologies. Key working principles are described and an optimal design strategy for the proposed APD converter is explored. Finally, simulation results for a 400 V, 3.45 k W battery charger topology (with a resistor used to emulate the battery load) is shown to validate the proposed concept and provide comparative results.

articleTitle: A Case Study for Standalone Solar Power Modules with and Without IoT Devices in Rural Hospital Emergency Rooms Located inKaniyambadi
abstract: Remote hospitals' critical infrastructure requires an uninterrupted power supply 24 hours a day, so power outages and natural disasters can have serious consequences because electricity from the utility grid cannot get there all the time. In emergencies, standalone (Islanded) solar panels, battery storage systems (BSS), and Internet of Things (IoT) devices work together to provide a reliable source to the patients, particularly in the emergency ward, and also save public life without stopping the treatment due to power failure. Standalone Solar Power Modules (SSPM) are installed in a remote hospital located at Kaniyambadi Village, Vellore district, Tamil Nadu, India, and it is taken as a case study for 1 year. The various readings are taken for the first 6 months without IoT sensors in SSPM, and other readings are taken for the next 6 months with IoT sensors. This paper discusses the two results: SSPM with IoT sensors will yield 82% efficiency, system stability, proper monitoring, and performance improvement, while the existing system (first 6 months) without IoT can only yield 63%. The major aim of this work is to save lives in remote hospitals by incorporating SSPM, BSS, and IoT sensors, which can increase by 19% and provide continuous supply to the hospitals.

articleTitle: On MATLAB-based Stability Analysis of Discrete Differential Capacitor Voltage Feedback for Active Damping of LCL Filters
abstract: Active damping of LCL filter with capacitor voltage feedback poses design and implementation challenge since a pure differentiator cannot be replicated exactly in the digital domain. Different approximations are used for implementing the discrete differentiator, whose behaviour (particularly phase contribution) often deviates from its continuous domain counterpart. Hence the performance guaranteed by the control system, designed in continuous domain, won't be delivered by the digital implementation. The paper proposes a virtual-impedance model for two of the discretization methods - (i) backward Euler approximation, and (ii) backward Euler approximation with lead compensator, to aid in the design and stability analysis of the converter control system in continuous domain. With the equivalent virtual impedance model, the feedback gain for active damping can be designed appropriately in continuous domain itself, and the designed value can be implemented in the discrete domain, without compromising the system performance. Simulation studies, done in MATLAB/Simulink based on the proposed approach are provided to substantiate the efficacy of the method.

articleTitle: A Nonisolated Enhanced Voltage Gain Dual Input DC-DC Converter with Symmetrical Bipolar Output
abstract: This paper introduces a novel four-port DC-DC converter designed for hybrid energy integration. The proposed non-isolated circuit topology provides a symmetrical bipolar output with enhanced voltage gain. It is specifically designed to interface Solar PV and fuel cells with a Bipolar DC microgrid, enabling single-stage energy conversion. The power converter features a simplified circuit structure with fewer components compared to existing high-gain multiport converters. Furthermore, it effectively controls inductor current and balances both pole voltages using a single set of controllers. A small-signal model is deduced for each operating state to facilitate the design of the control system. Steady-state and transient results are presented to validate the efficacy of the proposed circuit topology.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Model Predictive Controller for an Integrated Dual-DC Boost Converter
abstract: Multi-port dc-dc converters find significance in applications such as renewable integration, and hybrid- source systems. Power flow control and its management is one of the major challenges associated with multi-port converters. This work proposes a hybrid model predictive controller for control of power within the integrated dual dc boost converter topology. This topology is a three-port converter with one bidirectional port (suitable for an energy buffer, eg. battery). Due to sharing of control duty ratio using the same set of controllable switches, using separate controllers for each control objective results in cross-regulation within the different ports. This work presents the model predictive controller which can simplify control design for the multi-port system and hence provide robustness to the regulated system. The design of the controller and its evaluation is presented in this work.

articleTitle: Size – Efficiency Multi-Objective Design of DC-Link Capacitor in Two-Stage Single-Phase Converters
abstract: In a single-phase grid-connected two-stage converter with power factor correction, the design of the DC-link capacitor possesses a fundamental trade-off between the capacitor size and efficiency. Larger energy storage capacitors reduce the double-line frequency ripple to ensure a stable voltage for the DC-DC stage improving its soft-switched performance and efficiency. However, this advantage comes at the expense of a larger capacitor size. This work aims to find the optimal value of the capacitor value that balances the above two performance matrices. Specifically, a multi-objective design optimization is followed to identify Pareto solutions for a 3.3 kW, 48 V electric vehicle charger interfaced with the single-phase grid.

articleTitle: GaN Device Modelling Using Machine Learning Approach for Power Electronic Converters
abstract: This paper introduces a deep learning-based approach for modelling various GaN -based power electronic devices, crucial for designing and simulating diverse power electronic circuits and conducting performance analysis. The deep learning model is trained using different voltage, current levels, gate resistances, and parasitic inductances. The training dataset is obtained by simulating a realistic Double Pulse Test (DPT) circuit, considering parasitic elements. A many to many Long Short-Term Memory based deep learning model is designed to effectively capture complex switching behavior of GaN devices. This model enables efficient analysis of switching voltage and current, along with reliability assessment of GaN-based power converters. The accuracy of the proposed model is verified by comparing the LTspice simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive On-Time Average Current Control Tracking in Critical Conduction Mode Three- Level Boost PFC
abstract: Constant on-time (COT) modulation is popular among boost and totem-pole power factor correction (PFC) circuits under critical conduction mode (CrM) of operation due to its inherent average current tracking ability while achieving unity power factor. However, the same technique cannot be directly used for a flying capacitor-based multilevel boost PFC under the CrM operation because of different circuit configurations for different switching states. On the other hand, multilevel boost PFC converters with high frequency and low voltage GaN devices have been gaining growing interest for their high power density and high efficiency. This paper proposes an adaptive on-time modulation technique for a three-level flying capacitor boost PFC (3LFCB-PFC) under the CrM operation, ensuring its average current tracking ability. The expressions for the required on-time for different duty ratio ranges are analytically derived. These expressions are easily implementable using the input and output voltages and load current. A comparative study shows the reduction in the effective switching frequency of the 3LFCB- PFC circuit compared to the conventional two-level counterpart. The simulation results verify a superior tracking performance. The proposed technique will help to design compact power supplies/ chargers for LED drivers, data centers, electric vehicles, telecom servers, etc.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Digital Twins for Monitoring the Health and Performance of Converters
abstract: This work introduces a machine learning approach for developing Digital Twins (DTs) for DC-DC converters, focusing on in-situ implementation in real-world operational conditions. A system based on a boost converter has been developed in MATLAB Simulink. To mirror real-world scenarios, commercial datasheets along with a range of input parameters, health degradation elements, temperature influence, and random noises have been considered. The study employs Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for predicting critical circuit responses of the boost converter, including inductor current, output voltage, and efficiency. Investigations show that MLP performs relatively poorly in the presence of noise. The CNN and RNN outperform the MLP under various noise levels, with the RNN exhibiting the best performance. This work advances DTs technology in power electronics, aiming to improve converter system optimization and enable predictive maintenance.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of Fault-Tolerant Boost Inverter Topology
abstract: With the use of a high number of components in the multilevel converters, the chances of converter failure due to malfunction in components are high leading to reduced reliability and performance. In this paper, a new converter topology along with the fault-tolerant configuration which can be operated in two modes of operation has been proposed which incorporates the boosting feature as well. A detailed analysis for considering the faults in different switches for different modes of operation has been analyzed. Simulation results have been presented in this paper to show the performance and efficacy of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: LC Type dv/dt Filter Design with Clamping Diodes for SiC MOSFET-based Motor Drives
abstract: Ultrafast semiconductors such as Silicon Carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) have enabled the development of highly efficient and compact power electronic systems. These devices have very short rise and fall times, leading to very high rates of change of voltage (dv / dt), which can cause overvoltages in motor drive applications with long cables. This can result in winding insulation failure, bearing failure, increased common mode currents, and Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). Hence, mitigating the harmful effects of switching dv / dt is crucial. This paper presents an improved analysis and design procedure for an LC-type dv / dt filter with a diode clamp at the inverter output to attenuate overvoltages at the motor terminals. The proposed design approach aims to simultaneously minimize the size of the filter inductors as well as the filter losses. The filter's effectiveness is confirmed through switching circuit simulations. A hardware prototype of a 2-level Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) along with an LC-type dv / dt filter with clamping diodes is constructed in the laboratory. Experimental results are presented to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Development of Wireless Charging Systems for Intraoral Devices using Ultra-small Receiving Coils
abstract: In this paper, a magnetic-resonant coupling wireless power transfer (WPT) method for intraoral devices with very small coil is proposed. The WPT method using transmitting and receiving coils has the advantage of being able to supply power without any wire connection regardless of location limitation. This study designs and develop a wireless charging system to supply power of intraoral device, which is consist of a receiving coil, rectifier, sensor, and micro controller unit (MCU). The considered intraoral device are inserted inside teeth as dental implants. The power required for these dental devices is calculated by current consumption of each device. And, a simple prototype of transmitting and receiving circuit using ultra small coils are implemented and tested. Experimental results show that the proposed wireless charging system can supply power to intraoral device.

articleTitle: Impact of Deadband on a Three-Phase Three-Level NPC Inverter for Induction Motor Drive utilizing a Innovative Deadband Circuit
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative dead band circuit designed to be utilized in multilevel converters. Multilevel con-verters are workforce of industrial drive. Especially neutral point clamped (NPC) is very popular, and it has very high efficiency. To drive a three-phase three-level NPC (TTNPC) inverter, deadband circuits are utilised to avoid shoot-through between two switches in same leg of an inverter. In this article, Modelling and hardware implementation of an NPC inverter are carried out, and a fully controlled dead-band circuit is proposed using digital logic gates and RC circuits. Hardware is tested with carrier-based Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) Techniques, In-Phase Sinusoidal PWM (IPSPWM), and Phase Opposite SPWM (POSPWM). Experimental results demonstrate that deadband circuit exhibits minimal oscillation during dead band time, improving converter performance. Furthermore, performance of proposed deadband circuit is evaluated based on voltage and current total harmonic distortion (THD), and typical results are presented.

articleTitle: An Isolated Multi Active Bridge Type Soft Switched AC-DC Boost PFC Converter
abstract: This paper proposes a circuit topology for inte-grating multiple DC ports with an AC grid with galvanic isolation between every port. The proposed circuit topology is a Multi-Active Bridge (MAB) type soft-switched AC-DC boost PFC converter. A control strategy suited for battery charging application is presented. A unified approach for modelling the converter for all operating modes and modulation strategies is presented, which is used to determine the power flow, AC port currents, and soft-switching bounds. Experimental results from a 500 W laboratory hardware prototype are presented to validate the converter operation and control strategy.

articleTitle: Extended High Efficiency Operation of Semi - Active Half-Bridge DC-DC Converter
abstract: The semi-active half-bridge converter (SAHBC) is a promising option for cost-competitive electric vehicle (EV) charging systems. However, the conversion efficiency of SAHBC is poor at part load conditions. This is attributed to the small duration of current supply to the output and large duration of circulating current in the transformer. This paper proposes an efficiency improvement technique to address this issue. The proposed technique is a combination of design of SAHBC and strategic changes in its switching frequency. The design of SAHBC selects the turns ratio and leakage inductance. Whereas, the switching frequency of SAHBC is strategically increased to enhance the duration of output current transfer. This increase in switching frequency is easily implementable due to complete ZVS and ZCS operation of the power devices. A step-by-step methodology for the proposed technique and its application to a 2.4 kW EV charger are included in the paper. The presented analysis shows that the proposed technique achieves up to 9.3 % improvement in conversion efficiency at part load conditions. The operation of proposed technique is also validated with the help of a 2.4 kW laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Flexible Busbar Solution for High Current Density Applications
abstract: As power demand usage at datacenters and other facilities like nuclear power plants, battery energy storage systems, telecommunications and industrial facilities increases exponentially, the use of cables both in the primary and secondary medium voltage and low voltage has become difficult to design and implement. These power distribution systems at facilities need to be designed with multiple parallel cables, rigid bus bar system or flexible bus bar systems. There has been significant attention given to these systems, now as these have advantages and limitations. There has been progress on the system and component design of these systems as well as attention given to the maintenance and operation. This paper discusses the advantages and limitations of cable connections, rigid bus bar connection and flexible bus bar connections for high current density applications. UL standards for the certification of these systems are being developed. The systems are tested to several IEC standards for attributes like insulation resilience, cable fixing suitability, electrical characteristics, flame resistance. Flexible bus bar systems offer an excellent solution for point to point connections in power distribution. Future developments on these system may see its application extended to provide load distribution capabilities.

articleTitle: A Four-Port DC-DC Converter for Hybrid Integration of Fuel Cell-Solar PV with Bipolar DC Microgrid
abstract: This article describes a novel non-isolated dual-input dual-output DC-DC converter designed for the hybrid integration of Fuel Cell and Solar PV into bipolar DC microgrid systems, enabling single-stage power conversion. Unlike existing non-isolated multiport DC-DC converters, the proposed design offers significant voltage gain with fewer magnetic components. By employing a set of deduced controllers, the proposed converter effectively regulates both inductor current and output voltage, while its symmetrical output structure naturally balances pole voltages. Additionally, the converter can operate as a single-input-dual-output system if either the Fuel Cell or Solar PV source is unavailable. The paper explores various operating modes and presents steady-state simulation results, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: Non Conductive Gun for Electric Vehicle Charging
abstract: Conductive charging through a charging gun re-quires physical connection with the on-board power electronics with the limitation of proper handling during insertion and removal. Present paper utilizes the concept of wireless power transfer (WPT) to overcome the limitation with the conventional charging gun. A concept of non-conductive charging gun is introduced, where it consists of transmitting coils and com-pensation arrangement receiving energy from the grid and is termed as non conductive charging gun. Receiving coil remains the part of the on-board vertically mounted arrangement with the vehicle submitting energy to on-board battery pack through high-frequency rectifier and buck converter to inject controlled charging current. A 3.3kW@320V non conductive charging gun is sized and the operational validation is carried out through simulation.

articleTitle: DC Bus Regulation and Suppression of Circulating Current in an Isolated DC Microgrid
abstract: This paper addresses load current sharing, DC bus regulation, and circulating current issues of parallel-connected DC-DC converters in an isolated DC microgrid environment. Droop control is a popular technique for load current sharing in a DC microgrid. The main drawbacks of the conventional droop method are poor current sharing and a drop in DC grid voltage due to the droop action. Circulating current issues will also arise due to mismatches in the converter's output voltages. This work introduces a hierarchical control strategy to improve the performance of the DC microgrid. Integral sliding mode control and droop control are used at the primary layer, while an average voltage controller and an outer voltage regulator are used at the secondary layer. Sliding mode control, distinguished by its robustness and fast dynamic response, is utilised to manipulate the output voltage and the input current of each converter simultaneously, and hence it can also provide protection against over-current. Furthermore, at the secondary layer, an average voltage controller is added with a dedicated outer voltage control loop. The average voltage controller reduces the circulating current by equalising the converter output voltage, while the outer voltage control loop regulates the DC bus voltage of the microgrid by shifting the droop lines. In the proposed scheme, only the converter output voltage and DC bus voltage of the microgrid need to be transmitted through low-bandwidth communication channels to individual units. The dynamic performance of the proposed control scheme is evaluated using the MATLAB simulation environment.

articleTitle: Comparison of Current Control Techniques for Single-Phase Integrated On-Board Chargers
abstract: In recent years, due to high rise in deployment of electric vehicles in markets, battery chargers are high in demands. Chargers are generally of two types: on-board and off-board chargers. But in addition to above, in recent years integrated chargers have gained popularity amongst researchers in which the same motor and it's associated converter are used for both propulsion and charging modes. In this paper, comparative analysis has been done for different fixed switching frequency current controllers for single-phase integrated chargers. This control strategies are validated using simulations studies conducted using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Detailed Experimental Switching Transient Performance Comparison of Normally-off GaN HEMTs
abstract: GaN HEMTs offer a viable replacement for silicon counterparts due to their superior switching and conduction loss performances. Commercially available normally-off high-voltage (600 - 650V) GaN HEMTs can be broadly divided into (a) Cascode GaN, (b) e-GaN, and (c) GaN GIT. Due to differences in device characteristics and gate driving requirements, the switching dynamics of these GaN HEMTs can vary significantly. This paper focuses on experimental investigations comparing the switching behavior of these normally-off GaN HEMTs. High voltage GaN HEMTs (600 - 650V) with a current rating of about 30A are considered for comparison. Double pulse tests are conducted, and the switching transients are obtained for a wide range of operating conditions. The key switching transient-related parameters, such as switching losses, transition times, (di / dt), (dv / dt), etc., are also compared. The results offer valuable insights for the optimal selection of GaN HEMTs in various power electronics applications.

articleTitle: DC Microgrids Enabled with Triple Active Bridge Converter for Remote Areas
abstract: This paper presents a DC microgrid (DC MG) architecture to supply critical power to remote field areas. The DC MG is deployed by integrating PV and ESS, which are integrated together using a Triple Active Bridge Converter. The use of DC MG, particularly with parallel TAB converters, is presented as a promising solution to improve system reliability, scalability, and efficiency. The paper outlines the architecture and control strategies using the TAB converter, demonstrating its capability to regulate the DC bus voltage under varying solar conditions and dynamic load changes. The prototype demonstrates the potential benefits of DC microgrids in various applications, including remote areas and critical facilities such as healthcare institutions.

articleTitle: Comparison of Single-Phase GaN HEMT-based PFC Topologies for Onboard EV Chargers
abstract: A standard onboard charger typically consists of two stages, wherein the power factor correction (PFC) acts as the initial stage. This study explores various bridgeless PFC topologies - bridgeless totem-pole PFC (BTPFC), interleaved BTPFC, and H-bridge with sine-triangle PWM (SPWM) - suitable for a 3kW power rating. 650 V gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT) devices, known for their superior switching characteristics and thermal performance, are used in these PFC topologies. This research provides a comprehensive analysis of the distinct losses encountered in each PFC topology, including conduction losses, switching losses, dead time losses, and partial hard turn-on losses. Taking into account a bridge loss limit of 1 - 1.5% of total power and a thermal limit of 70% of the maximum junction temperature, the paper presents a detailed selection of switching frequency for the PFC topologies. Additionally, it provides a comparison of boost inductors and filter capacitors based on the chosen switching frequency.

articleTitle: Accurate Efficiency Estimation of DC/DC Converters using Automatic Temperature Calibration
abstract: An accurate efficiency estimation method ensures proper device selection, thermal design and facilitates further optimization of the design without repeated experimentations. A Temperature Calibrated Efficiency Estimation Method (TCEEM) is proposed in this paper which estimates the efficiency without prior experimentation. The proposed method accounts for the temperature rise in the semiconductor device thus producing better estimations. The proposed algorithm is verified experimentally on a Si-based and a GaN-based 120 W synchronous buck converter. The application of the algorithm in switch selection is also discussed.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Approach to Addressing the Lightning and Grounding Safety Requirements in Grid-Integrated EES Systems Per IEC 62933-5-2
abstract: This paper reviews lightning and grounding safety requirements in grid-integrated BESS systems per IEC 62933 part 5-2: Safety requirements for grid-integrated electrical energy storage (EES) systems - Electrochemical-based systems. Based on the IEC 62933-5-2 recommendations, a lightning protection risk assessment is carried out using the methodology descibed in IEC 62305–2. Lightning protection measures compliant to IEEE 998:2012 are implemented in response to the results of the risk assessment. The captured lightning current is dissipated into the earthing grid built under the EES system and nearby transformers. Grid resistivity and safety assessments are carried (step and touch hazards) out for various faults (short-circuit) scenarios using IEEE 80:2013. It is shown that modelling of the nearby HV substation and PV farm, when present, is important as it will lead to a more precise assessment of the electrocution risk on the BESS side. This assessment allows for increased safety while limiting costly over-design of safety measures.

articleTitle: Adaptive Model Predictive Control Applying on Two-Switch Forward Converter for the Application of High Voltage Battery Management System
abstract: The two-switch forward converter (TSFC) is controlled by using Adaptive Model Predictive Control (A - MPC). Due to its multiple objective and constraint handling ability, this type of controller is suitable for a broad range of input voltage applications, such as DC supply for an electronic subsystem in a high-voltage Battery Management System (BMS). A-MPC controls the output voltage in the presence of model uncertainties. This research work presents an in-depth analysis of converter modelling and control. The proposed A - MPc control strategy is implemented in a MATLAB simulation environment to test its efficacy and robustness. The proposed A-MPC control strategy works better as compared to PI controller and second-order sliding mode controller known as super twisting control (STC).

articleTitle: Analysis and Design for Current Balancing in Interleaved LLC Converters for Two-Stage DCX 48-to-1V Telecom Power Supply
abstract: Multi-phase interleaved LLC (MPILLC) converters are predominantly used as a fixed-gain high power density DC transformer (DCX) with high output current in the first stage of an intermediate bus architecture. This is particularly useful in 48-to-PoL (point of load) converters in data centers and telecom power supplies. By suitably designing the power stage, operating at the resonant frequency, and applying phase shift among individual phases, an MPILLC converter can achieve phase current balancing with reduced ripple voltage, which can also retain high efficiency over a wide load current range by utilizing the soft switching capability. However, this paper shows that small changes in tank parameters lead to significant phase current imbalance. Thereafter, an analytical framework is developed by considering the first harmonic approximation (FHA) technique to analyze the effect of parameter mismatches on individual phase currents. The framework is further extended to utilize the duty ratio as the control degree of freedom for balancing phase currents under a wide variation of power-stage parameters. Simulation results of a two-phase LLC converter are presented to demonstrate the accuracy of the analytical predictions as well as the usefulness of the proposed approach. The proposed technique can be extended to an increasing number of phase counts.

articleTitle: A PSIM-Based Tool for Quick Failure Rate Estimation for a DC-DC Converter
abstract: We are witnessing nowadays an increasing attention to reliability aspects in electronic circuits, especially in the field of Power Electronics. Practitioners in particular have increasingly found a need for rapid evaluation of two fundamental metrics of reliability, MTBF and failure rate. This paper proposes a tool for quick estimation of changes in the lifetime or reliability of a dc-dc converter when various design parameters are changed in practice. This is useful for critical power systems since it allows the maintenance planning when lifetime, reliability, or MTBF changes due to inappropriate use of the dc/dc converter. Experimental validation uses for validation a demo board with a Point-of-Load converter type POL-EVB-514390 from Silicon labs, which is equipped with n-channel MOSFETs HAT2185 from Renesas Semiconductor. Tests included variation in load current and switching frequency. The simulation section uses certain dedicated thermal models from the PSIM simulation program library.

articleTitle: Design of Three-Phase Multi-Winding Transformer of High-Frequency AC Power Distribution Architecture for Space Application
abstract: This paper presents a detailed design of a high-frequency three-phase (3ϕ) multi-winding transformer tailored for space applications. Using high-frequency converters is paramount to minimize the footprint of passive components and optimize power distribution architecture, which are critical considerations for satellite power systems. Furthermore, the complexity of designing a multi-winding transformer on a single core necessitates meticulous attention to ensure compactness. This study outlines a comprehensive design methodology for a 10kHz, 100W, 3ϕ multi-winding transformer. The design approach is validated through simulation using ANSYS Maxwell 3D, providing corresponding results. Additionally, experimental validation is conducted by delivering 100 W of power through a 10 kHz 3ϕ high-frequency AC system, affirming the practical viability of the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Switched-Sink Bidirectional Power Amplifier
abstract: Power Hardware in Loop (PHIL) methodology enables the flexible and risk-free testing of physical equipment. A power amplifier (PA) is essential to interface the RT simulator with the Hardware under Test (HuT). This application requires the PA to have bidirectional power transfer capability. Therefore, conventional power amplifiers cannot be used directly. The paper proposes an alternate solution to build a two-stage power amplifier with a bidirectional power flow capability. The novelty of the proposed solution is two-fold. First, a novel switched-power sink is incorporated into the PA structure to accommodate reverse power flow. Secondly, a control scheme for the switched power sink is proposed to achieve seamless transfer between the forward and reverse power modes. This switched-sink architecture provides a low-cost, low-complexity solution that is ideal for low-power applications. The operation of the proposed switched-sink PA architecture with a seamless control algorithm is verified in a lab-developed prototype.

articleTitle: A Feedforward Control Methodology Incorporating Input and Output Voltage Variations in Dual Active Bridge Converter
abstract: In a typical data centre application, utilization of DC distribution system by generating a HV-DC bus (800V) is becoming increasingly popular for improved distribution efficiency. For this, the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter is increasingly being considered for the isolated DC/DC converter stage. One important requirement of such an application is the tight regulation of output HV-DC bus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{o})$</tex> irrespective of load and input DC voltage changes. In this paper, a input and output voltage feed-forward based control scheme is proposed, considering the power flow analysis from both primary and secondary sides. The proposed feed-forward method is found to be inherent in a DAB converter operation. The proposed feed-forward method is incorporated in the traditional two-loop control of DAB converter. Through analytical, simulation studies and experimental validation, the proposed scheme is compared against two loop control and is found to have improved the transient performance of the DAB converter.

articleTitle: A Fault-Tolerant Single-Phase Inverter Using Redundant Leg
abstract: Single-phase inverters are increasingly used in a variety of applications from renewable energy systems to un-interruptible power supply. In the design and operation of these inverters, reliability remains a major concern. The single-phase inverter offers fault tolerance by including a redundant leg. The conventional redundant leg configuration uses four triode for alternating current (TRIAC) and two switches. The voltage seen across TRIACs used to connect the redundant leg is pulse width modulated (PWM). The high dv/dt across the TRIACs in the conventional topology due to PWM causes spurious turn ON across TRIACs. It leads to a short-circuit (SC) across the terminals. Thus, there is a need to modify the conventional TRIAC arrangement that is used to connect the redundant leg. In this paper, an updated TRIAC arrangement for a fault-tolerant single-phase inverter is proposed. The proposed TRIAC arrangement uses a split inductor filter to provide a sinusoidal voltage across the TRIACs. Thus the rearrangement of TRIAC ensures the lower dv/dt across the terminals. The reconfiguration of TRIACs is verified in simulation and experimentally through a 200V single-phase inverter with redundant leg prototype.

articleTitle: A Reduced Switching State PWM Single-Stage 3-Phase Matrix Inverter Without Device Voltage Spikes
abstract: This research introduces a novel topology and modulation for a single-stage three-phase high-frequency isolated matrix inverter designed to eliminate voltage spikes on the AC side without resorting to traditional clamp circuits. The proposed converter incorporates a modified full bridge on the DC side, creating a step voltage across the transformer secondary to effectively eliminate voltage spikes. Additionally, an innovative modulation strategy is employed on the matrix converter, which would help in the complete elimination of the voltage spike across the devices. The number of switching transitions of the matrix converter employing the proposed modulation strategy would be less than the conventional modulation strategies. Therefore, the switching losses would be less in the proposed solution. The proposed converter also achieves reduced RMS currents and enables soft-switching in most devices, contributing to an overall increase in efficiency and reduced current and voltage stress on the devices.

articleTitle: Aging-Aware Equivalent Circuit Model for SOH Estimation in Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Li-ion battery internal impedance is a crucial pa-rameter for state of health estimation. In this paper, a 3RC equivalent circuit model of the battery is considered. This model is also able to simulate the aging of the battery by extracting the battery parameter dependencies with aging. By observing the changes in the model parameters, it is possible to extract the battery state of heath. This means that starting from an impedance measurement it is possible to estimate the state of health of the battery. This could be a very attractive solution for the battery swapping industry, where keeping track of the aging can help identify early signs of degradation or potential safety hazards, thereby increasing customer satisfaction, optimizing operational efficiency and maximizing the return of investment. In this work, a neural network for state of health estimation from internal resistance is developed and it is able to correctly estimate state of health with a mean absolute relative error of 4.25%

articleTitle: Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Data-Driven Approach for EV Charging and Discharging Scheduling Problem
abstract: This paper presents Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient approach as a model-free deep reinforcement learning method for the management of electric vehicles (EVs) charging and discharging processes through vehicle-to-grid technology in the intent to minimize the charging cost from an EV owner perspective and provide peak-shaving services to reduce the strains on the power grid infrastructure due to uncontrolled charging of EVs. The scheduling problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) which serves as a representation of this complex decision making problem and solved by utilizing DDPG as a data-driven approach. The goal is to learn an optimal deterministic policy that enables charging actions during valley hours and discharging during peak hours while considering the driving demand of the EV owner and the variability in driving patterns, arrival and departure times, and the EV battery state of charge.

articleTitle: Prediction and Mitigation of Common Mode Noise in a Four-Switch Buck-Boost Converter
abstract: The Four-Switch Buck-Boost (FSBB) converter can function as a buck, boost, or buck-boost converter and employ various modulation schemes to reduce the electrical stresses of active and passive components and enhance efficiency. However, switching power devices in the FSBB converter generate electromagnetic interference (EMI), influenced by factors such as modulation techniques and the physical layout of the converter. There is a need to address EMI - related aspects during the design phase to ensure compliance with standards and avoid costly design changes and repetitive EMI tests. This paper proposes an equivalent circuit-based analytical model to predict conducted emissions from an FSBB converter. The simplified model aids the first-pass EMI filter design process. A hardware prototype of the FSBB converter is constructed. EMI measurements are presented from pre-compliance tests conducted at the laboratory to validate the effectiveness of proposed modelling and filter design approaches.

articleTitle: High Efficient, High Power Intensive DC-DC Converter Solution for 5G Telecom
abstract: The 5G networks are causing a notable shift in the Telecom Power System Market. The higher power requirements and increased network distribution associated with 5G technology drive the demand for more advanced and adaptable power solutions. There is a growing market demand to enhance the power capacity of the converter without changing the physical dimensions (1U x 2U size) to accommodate the transition from 4G to 5G technology. Generally, regular rectifiers provide the isolation between AC mains and DC supply. So, there is no need to design isolated converters in telecom applications. This DC-DC converter provides non-isolated output with >97.5% efficiency and a peak power capacity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$70\mathrm{W}/\text{in}^{3}$</tex>. With a focus on energy efficiency, the market is incorporating energy-saving technologies such as advanced rectifiers, efficient cooling systems, and intelligent power management solutions. These energy-efficient telecom power systems not only lower operational expenses but also help in reducing carbon emissions. This DC-DC converter consists of two identical boost converters connected in parallel and controlled by the interleaved method which has the same switching frequency and phase shift. The boost voltage helps offset the voltage drop across the load lines connected to the radios. As a result, it enables extended battery operation during power outages. The advantages of interleaved boost converters include increased efficiency, reduced size, and improved reliability. This paper presents, the design and implementation of a two-phase interleaved boost converter.

articleTitle: Analysis of Overvoltage Across Blanking Capacitor Due to Junction Capacitance of Sensing Diode in Desat Protection of SiC MOSFET
abstract: Wide-band-gap devices exhibit rapid switching capabilities, enhancing conversion efficiency and reducing converter size. However, their low short circuit withstand time (SCWT) capacity necessitates swift and precise fault detection and protection mechanisms. The reduction in fault detection time in desaturation (Desat) based protection requires minimising blanking capacitance. When the blanking capacitance is comparable to the sensing diode junction capacitance, the reverse recovery current of the sensing diode and oscillations across the device lead to overvoltage across the blanking capacitor during device turn-off and discontinuous current mode (DCM) operation, respectively, which leads to spurious fault detection. Based on variable junction capacitance of sensing diode, this paper presents an analytical method to estimate overvoltage across blanking capacitor during turn-off. This paper also derives a transfer function relating the device voltage oscillations with blanking capacitor voltage oscillations during DCM, which shows the impact of reduced blanking capacitance on overvoltage. Simulations and experiments validate the accuracy of the analytical methods proposed. Additionally, a recently proposed voltage clamping method is implemented to clamp such overvoltages, and experimental results on an 800-V(dc), 50-A(rms), and 50-kHz asymmetric H-bridge (AHB) converter are presented.

articleTitle: PSAM and TM Based Fault Tolerant Scheme for Open Switch Faults in Dual Active Bridge Converters
abstract: Dual active bridges (DABs) are widely utilized in solid-state transformers (SSTs) and energy storage systems. The reliability of an isolated DAB converter is critically dependent on its performance under various fault conditions, with open switch faults (OSFs) being a predominant issue. This study introduces an innovative fault-tolerant scheme for DAB DC-DC converters to address OSFs on both the primary and secondary sides. The proposed method integrates phase shift angle modulation (PSAM) along with topology modifications (TM). Initially, the operational behavior of the DAB under normal conditions, as well as under primary and secondary switch OSFs, is analyzed. Based on this analysis, PSAM, and TM techniques is proposed to address OSFs, focusing particularly on faults occurring in switches S1 and S5. The proposed fault-tolerant scheme is capable of transmitting 75% of the nominal power during primary side OSFs and approximately 98% during secondary side OSFs, thereby ensuring continued safe operation. The effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed scheme for managing OSFs are validated through MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: A Review of High-Voltage High-Step Down Isolated Converter Topologies
abstract: In this paper, various isolated topologies with high buck ratio, suitable for High Voltage (HV) power electronics systems are reviewed. A brief comparative analysis is carried out in terms of important performance indices, such as efficiency, size, and cost. From the analysis, a novel Asymmetric Half Bridge (AHB) topology is proposed which is most suitable solution for HV power electronics systems. The proposed topology has advantages in terms of improved power density and higher efficiency over conventionally used converters for high buck applications. Hence, steady state operation of the topology is verified experimentally at different operating points.

articleTitle: Secondary Side-Controlled Fly-Back Converter for USB PD Charger Application
abstract: Universal serial bus power delivery (USB-PD) charg-ers are gaining popularity due to their versatility. However, these chargers have design challenges such as high-power density, full and light load efficiencies and tight regulations across a wide input and output voltage range as per PD specifications. This paper proposes a novel secondary side-controlled fly-back converter approach using PAG2S and PAG2P ICs from Infineon Technologies. The architecture integrates three key functions for PD chargers using just two ICs, whereas state of the art solution requires 3 ICs to achieve these functions. This paper presents the architecture of a PD charger using the unique combination of PAG2P and PAG2S ICs, suitable for all high efficiency fly-back configurations like Active clamp fly-back (ACF), Quasi resonance zero voltage switching (QR ZVS), and Quasi resonance (QR). A PAG2S and PAG2P based 65W charger with Cool GaN FET and ACF topology is used to demonstrate the advantage of integration, achieving a high power density of 32. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathrm{W}/\text{inch}^{3}$</tex> for Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA), peak efficiency of over 94.5 %, and EuP lot6 v2 compliance for light load efficiency

articleTitle: Performance of a Doubly Excited Cylindrical Rotor Brushless Synchronous Generator
abstract: In this work, a doubly excited cylindrical rotor brushless synchronous generator is proposed. The machine consists of two-pole excitation winding in both the stator and rotor, along with the four-pole armature winding in the stator and field winding in the rotor. The excitation windings develop the required excitation for the field winding of the synchronous generator and are connected to the field winding in the rotor by a rotating three-phase diode bridge rectifier. However, the excitation winding in the rotor is kept in such a way that the current flowing in the excitation winding develops some extra 4-pole Flux in the core, which in turn boosts up the voltage induced in the main machine armature. Thus, the flux produced by the excitation machine is utilized to develop armature voltage in the main machine(MM). This phenomenon improves voltage regulation and also reduces field current rating of the synchronous generator. In this work, a 5 kVA, 415 V machine is designed and its no load and full load characteristics are obtained from Ansys Maxwell 2D.

articleTitle: A New Integrated Onboard Battery Charger For Electric Scooters
abstract: In this paper a new DAB based bidirectional integrated onboard charger for electric scooters is discussed. Utilizing a single-phase matrix converter as a high-frequency AC-AC converter, a high-frequency transformer as isolation, and incorporates semiconductors from the onboard traction inverter as rectifiers to efficiently charge the low-voltage battery. For enhanced safety, high-frequency isolation safeguards the internal traction circuit. Additionally, the onboard electric motor is disengaged during the charging process to protect unintentional power flow. A design example implementing optimal Triple Phase Shift (TPS) modulation with 4-step switching, and minimum RMS current technique is showcased, featuring a 3kW power rating and benchmarking this rating against a conventional off-the-shelf external charger. This approach promises improved integration and convenience in electric scooter charging solutions.

articleTitle: A Non-Isolated Modified Quadratic DC-DC Boost Converter in a Stacked Configuration with Reduced Switch Voltage Stress
abstract: This paper proposes a non-isolated modified Quadratic DC-DC Boost Converter (mQBC) in a stacked configuration with reduced switch voltage stress while drawing continuous input current. Conventional Quadratic DC-DC Boost Converter (QBC) consists of an active switch, three diodes, two inductors, and two capacitors. However, the voltages across the active switch and the output capacitor are same as the output voltage. The proposed mQBC topology is primarily based on the conventional quadratic boost converter while replacing one of the three diodes with an active switch. Different modes of operation have been explained, and steady-state analysis of the mQBC in continuous conduction mode (CCM) has been done, incorporating the voltage stress across the components and non-ideal voltage gain. A comparative analysis with existing literature is also presented. A dual-loop control strategy is employed to regulate the output voltage of mQBC irrespective of dynamic load variations and changes in input voltage. MATLAB simulation results have been provided to validate the operation and performance of mQBC.

articleTitle: Analyzing Impact of Current Distribution on Parallel Connected Battery Packs in Telecom Applications
abstract: Telecommunication networks rely heavily on robust and reliable power systems as back-up to ensure uninterrupted service. In order to meet the desired load, multiple low voltage (LV) packs are connected in parallel. While research has been conducted on parallel-connected cells, there is a noticeable gap in the literature concerning parallel-connected packs. This research paper investigates the intricacies of parallel connected low voltage Li-ion battery packs for telecom application, with a primary focus on understanding and analyzing current variations across the battery packs during different scenarios. The study examines current distribution when a new battery pack is connected in parallel with older packs with lesser charge capacity. The paper further explores current distribution when slight capacity variation is present in the packs. Also, it investigates the effects of SOC imbalance on the current distribution in the packs. It was observed that the long-term life of the packs is affected if large initial state of health variation is present between the packs. For smaller variation in health and for SOC imbalance within the packs there is minimal influence on the health of the packs.

articleTitle: Indoor Grounding of Data Centers to IEC30129 and TIA607-E Standards
abstract: The indoor grounding system at a data center has been an evolving discipline from its inception in the early days where almost all data centers had a raised floor construction. Today raised floor designs are less common and more thought is needed in the design of indoor grounding systems. Standards IEC 30129 and AS 30129 Telecommunications Bonding Networks for Buildings and Other Structures and Standard TIA607-E Generic Telecommunications Bonding and Grounding (Earthing) for Customer Premises provide guidance on the design and installation of the indoor grounding systems suited for the modern datacenter. This paper will discuss the design requirements and common installation practices for the implementation of a good grounding system that would follow these guidelines. It will also discuss how the data center indoor grounding system is interfaced with other grounding systems like the low voltage or the LV ground, the high voltage or the HV grounding system, the DC Power grounding system and grounding system for any adjacent renewable energy source like photovoltaics. The key reasons for the design and installation of the grounding system are: •Noise and Transient Control •Fault-current mitigation •Equipment protection •Protection of people •Signal reference •Reducing effects of ground loops

articleTitle: Component Stress Minimization of Resonant DC/DC Converter Using Fractional Power Processing for Battery Charging
abstract: A fractional power processing architecture is presented in this paper enabling a solution to the high voltage and current stress issues across the resonant converters. The proposed configuration allows only a differential voltage and differential current to appear across the converter terminal thereby, reducing the voltage and current through the converter components. The converter is connected in an input parallel output series (IPOS) configuration with the battery load and available DC source, respectively. Thus, the proposed configuration of the converter reduces the losses and thereby improves the efficiency of the overall charger. Further, a reduction in size of heat sink and optimization in component rating makes it a cost-effective and compact solution. The proposed architecture is implemented using a DAB-derived current fed parallel resonant converter that maintains soft-switching for the entire range of operation. The design criterion of the proposed charger is presented. The constant current -constant voltage behavior of the proposed converter is verified through simulation. The suitability of the proposed solution for battery charging is verified using a 700 W lab developed prototype.

articleTitle: ZVS-Oriented Power Sharing Control in Modular DAB Converters Connected in Input-Parallel Output-Parallel Configuration
abstract: This paper presents an analytical formulation, implementation and validation of an intelligent load sharing algorithm capable of enhancing the zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) performance, applicable to an input-parallel output-parallel (IPOP) connected dual-active-bridge (DAB)-based modular dc-dc converter system. In this study, first, the critical inductor currents required to attain ZVS in the DAB switching legs are identified based on the non-linear body capacitor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(C_{oss})$</tex> of the switching devices, followed by synthesis of the critical ZVS power conditions. Then, the total system load is intelligently distributed among the DAB modules so that all the modules can independently experience soft-switching under any gain and load scenario. The proposed load sharing algorithm promises to showcase significant efficiency (~0.5-2%), and EMI benefit in DABs in IPOP configuration.

articleTitle: A Unified Reduced Order Modeling and Dual-Loop Frequency Control Design for CLLC Resonant Converter
abstract: This paper proposes a unified small-signal model of a dual active bridge (DAB)-based CLLC resonant converter, considering the internal phase shift in the primary bridge, the external phase shift between the two bridges, and the switching frequency as the model parameters. The extended describing function (EDF) concept and fundamental harmonic approximation (FHA)-based equivalent circuit simplifications are utilized to arrive at a third-order model of the converter, which provides all necessary control transfer functions. A 22 kW DAB-CLLC resonant converter, with input and output voltage ratings of 750 V and 400 V, respectively, verifies the proposed model. The control architecture features a dual-loop setup that comprises of internal current and external voltage loop, offering precise and efficient control. The external loop compensator generates a current reference for the internal loop based on the desired output voltage. The internal loop compensator modifies the switching frequency to match the current reference. The transient response of the designed compensator is analyzed, giving a settling time of 5 ms for both step loading and step change in output voltage reference. The control scheme is implemented using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Non-Isolated Interleaved High Step-Down DC-DC Converter with Reduced Switched Capacitor Stages and Automatic Current Sharing
abstract: A high-voltage dc power supply system is an attractive solution for reducing the system cost and improving efficiency. This system needs compact but high-efficiency high-step-down converters to exploit the benefits. This paper proposes a novel converter for a better candidate than traditional converters. The proposed converter is a non-isolated high step-down converter utilizing the switched capacitor technology. Compared to conventional similar topologies, the number of switched capacitor stages can be reduced, enabling the compact converter design. Furthermore, this converter has interleaved output, which can downsize the magnetic devices. The current of the interleaved output is automatically balanced without special control, enabling simple controller implementation. These features were successfully verified by the experiment.

articleTitle: An Interpolation based Synthetic Battery Data Generation Technique
abstract: Global collaborative efforts to mitigate environmental pollution has led to increased efforts to electrify the automotive sector. Lithium-ion batteries, one of the most predominant sources of energy, has been the primary driver of this green revolution to curb automotive pollutants. Accurate State-of-Charge evaluation of such Lithium-ion batteries has been a long standing research problem among energy researchers. There have been a series of solutions proposed in literature to compute precise State-of-Charge estimates, all of which assume accessibility to labelled battery datasets. In reality, researchers lack access to diverse datasets and battery manufacturers are unwilling to share proprietary datasets. In this paper, we tackle the issue of lack of high quality data by introducing a hierarchic interpolation synthetic data generation approach. Some of the key contributions of our work are: a) synthetic data generation using reliable interpolation method, b) we highlight the effectiveness of this approach by comparing it with other state-of-the-art synthetic data generation techniques. Code can be found at this URL: https://github.com/vageeshmaiya/Hierarchical-Interpolation

articleTitle: Frequency-and Time-Domain-Based Methods to Estimate Parasitic Capacitances in Planar Magnetics using Terminal Measurements
abstract: Planar magnetic structures integrated into printed circuit boards are becoming preferred in various applications due to their high repeatability, good thermal performance, and efficient winding patterns. However, these structures are prone to high parasitic capacitances, especially at very high frequen-cies, due to the proximity of different PCB layers. Estimating the impact of parasitic capacitance on planar inductors and transformers is crucial as it defines their operational frequency range. Existing methods for estimating parasitic capacitance rely on physics-based and finite-element-based approaches, requiring specific computational software and detailed winding geometry. This paper introduces two new capacitance estimation methods based on terminal measurements of planar magnetic components. One method utilizes frequency-domain characteristics while the other leverages time-domain properties, both formulated with an approximate equivalent circuit model derived from fundamental network analysis principles. Both methods are validated through application to a planar magnetic prototype, demonstrating con-sistent and reliable results.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 6/4 Switched Reluctance Motor for Solar Water Pumping System
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a three-phase, 1-horsepower 6/4 Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) for integration within a solar photovoltaic (SPV) array-driven water pumping system. The distinctive features of the SRM, such as high torque density, low inertia, swift response, and reduced losses attributed to the absence of permanent magnets or windings on the rotor, coupled with its extensive speed range capability and simplified control, render it a superior choice compared to DC and AC motors for SPV-powered water pumping applications. To seamlessly integrate the SPV array, a DC-DC boost converter is employed as an intermediary for maximum power extraction. The boost converter assumes a critical role in maintaining continuous and smooth input/output current, providing a wide operational range. Power is delivered to the SRM through the Asymmetrical Half-Bridge (AHB) converter, which effectively regulates phase voltage to achieve precise speed control of the drive. The design, modeling of SRM uses Ansys-Maxwell and simulation utilize MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A 300 VA Low-Cost Efficient Standalone Photovoltaic System for Rural Applications
abstract: With the ever-growing need for electricity, solar energy is becoming increasingly relevant. In rural India where the availability of grid is a challenge, the use of standalone PV systems is an attractive solution. This paper realizes a standalone PV system by combining all the power electronic units; maximum power point tracking controller, battery charger and inverter into one single unit. A novel control for the standalone operation of the PV system is proposed with minimal sensor requirements. The proposed control systematically detects different modes of operation based on the PV panel output, battery state of charge and the load demand. A prototype of 300 W standalone system capable of achieving an overall peak efficiency of greater than 85 % is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Diode Emulation Control for Efficiency Improvement of Dual Active Bridge Converters
abstract: The literature suggests discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) operation for efficiency improvement of dual active bridge (DAB) converters. These techniques require zero voltage across the primary side of the transformer to ensure DCM at part load conditions. Hence, these techniques are not implementable in cost-competitive DAB converters with half-bridge circuit on the primary side (cost-effective up to few kWs). This paper proposes diode emulation control (DEC) for DAB with half-bridge circuit on the primary side. The proposed technique ensures DCM at part load with a simple single phase shift control. The DEC is easily implemented with synchronous rectifier ICs, which are simple to use and popularly available. The design of transformer turns ratio and leakage inductance as per proposed technique are also added. The changes required in the closed loop control of the DAB due to diode emulation on secondary side are also highlighted. When compared to the conventional control, the proposed technique achieves up to 2.5 % improvement in efficiency at part load conditions. The proposed technique is experimentally validated with a 440 W laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive Control for Split DC-Link Based Dual Active Bridge Converter
abstract: This paper develops a Model Reference Adaptive Controller (MRAC) scheme for a split de-link dual-active-bridge (SDLDAB)-based multiport converter (MPC). The proposed controller's control parameters are adaptively adjusted as the converter parameters vary under different conditions. It does not require the state-space modelling of the converter, unlike in a conventional proportional-integral (PI) controller. By estimating the control parameters using an adaptation law, the performance of the MRAC is compared with a PI controller in order to illustrate the effectiveness and resilience of the adaptive operation. The developed method was tested on MATLAB/Simulink software.

Author Keywords: split dc-link based dual active bridge converter

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization of Current and Next-Generation Lithium-ion Battery for E-mobility Applications
abstract: Solid-state batteries (SSBs) offer promising advances in next-generation energy storage systems, exhibiting better safety, energy density, and longevity over traditional lithium-ion batteries. However, understanding and managing their thermal behavior across diverse operating conditions is vital to ensure reliable operation. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the thermal behavior of SSBs through laboratory experiments under controlled conditions. Furthermore, it examines the thermal characteristics of SSB under various charging and discharging conditions, assessing the suitability for e-mobility applications, in comparison to the traditional lithium nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) battery. The findings of this study provide valuable information for the development of thermal management strategies and the enhancement of the design, safety, and efficiency of SSB technologies for e-mobility applications.

articleTitle: Multi-winding Transformer based CLLC Current Mismatch Mitigation using Inter-bridge phase shift
abstract: High current side of resonant DC-DCs utilize multi-winding transformer structure to ease the current stress of semiconductor devices and avoid layout complexity encountered due to parasitic mismatch of multiple parallelled wide-band gap power devices. However, in practice, a slight variation in the leakage inductance values of such a transformer could lead to a notable variation in port current rms values leading to unequal power losses and non-uniform thermal stress, and possible device failures. In this paper, CLLC modeling and analysis is performed to study the impact of inter-bridge phase shift on the alleviation of non-uniform port current distribution. To benchmark the converter performance vis-a-vis the developed analytical model, a wide-bandgap devices-based 600V -28V 1.6 kW CLLC hardware prototype with a three-winding transformer and two paralleled secondary ports is developed for a resonant frequency of 500 kHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of Stray Capacitance Effects in Dynamics of LLC Converters under PFM for Battery Charging
abstract: In digital voltage mode-controlled LLC converter under pulse frequency modulation (PFM), a PID controller needs to be designed to achieve adequate transient performance under step changes in reference voltage, load current, and/or input voltage. However, the unevenly distributed high-frequency ringing and unpredictable voltage regulation issues caused by the stray capacitances cannot be predicted using the traditional fundamental harmonic approximation approach, which may lead to malfunctioning of the circuit components, degrade the transformer's lifespan, and cause devastating effects on the entire system. This paper highlights the typical potential threat that stray capacitances may introduce to the closed-loop dynamics of LLC converter and addresses the feasible degrees of freedom in order to minimize their influence on the converter's performance over a wide operating condition. Analytical predictions are verified using simulation results, and the performance improvement by conditionally adopting the dead time adjustment along with robust controller design is presented.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-driven Battery SOC Estimation for Electric Vehicle Application
abstract: The batteries are the main energy source in electric vehicles (EVs). Estimating the State of Charge (SOC) batteries is crucial for maximizing their performance and optimizing their range. This study proposes a unique approach using an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to estimate the SOC of batteries. This ANN model incorporates multiple hidden layers to capture the complex and nonlinear relationship between the terminal voltage and the SOC. The training is performed using the Levenberg Marquardt algorithm, known for its effectiveness in nonlinear regression and curve-fitting problems. The simulation is performed in MATLAB for a 12.8V, 7.5Ah battery, which considers variable current, temperature, and voltage as the input factor and provides SOC for different conditions. It is found that the ninth hidden layer in ANN achieves a minimal Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0027, which provides the optimal layer for training. Two charging methods are considered to check the effectiveness of the ANN model. The result shows predicted SOCs for Multi-step Constant Current and Constant Current Constant Voltage charging methods in this paper. Other parameters of batteries such as SOH, aging, safety, and protection can be predicted using ANN for EV applications.

articleTitle: Compact and Modular Power Units for Remotely Operated Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents an ISOP (Input-Series-Output-Parallel) modular architecture using interleaved isolated DC-DC power units with fault-tolerant capabilities to supply reliable power to subsea remotely operated vehicles (ROV s) at high system efficiency and power density. The proposed power converter units are constructed using a solid-state transformer (SST) for stepping down the medium voltage DC (MVDC) from the power umbilical to a lower voltage DC (LVDC) that can be used to power the ROV's thrusters, auxiliary loads, etc. A closed-loop control strategy of the output voltage and module current of the ROV's power unit with due consideration of “N-I” redundancy for fault tolerance of the system is proposed in this work. Interleaving of converter modules is also implemented to reduce the noise and hence the filter size. Real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) results based on a Typhoon HIL system are presented to verify the converter's operation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Real-Time Digital Control for Phase Shifted Full-Bridge Rectifier Using Texas Instruments' ARM Cortex-R5F Core Based MCU
abstract: Conditioning of digital power plays a crucial role in this era of booming electric vehicle (EV) and renewable energy harvesting industry. Most of these applications consist of two fundamental stage of power conversion. One is AC to DC conversion stage followed by a DC to DC conversion stage or vice-versa. Due to the ease of controllability, the phase shifted full-bridge (PSFB) rectifier is often selected as the go-to solution for transferring bulk amount of power from the high voltage (HV) DC to the low voltage (LV) DC side with electrical isolation. One such simple control scheme that can be used in this application is called peak current mode control (PCMC). The power transfer happens from the HV to LV side when the turn ON period of diagonally opposite switches of two legs overlap with each other. In PCMC, this overlapping period is controlled by setting the peak current value suitably. On top of this, an outer voltage control loop is implemented to maintain the output voltage at the desired level. In this work, the control mechanism is implemented using TMDSCNCD263 SITARA MCU of Texas Instruments (TI). This work showcases industry standard ARM Cortex-R5F core MCU based real-time digital control implementation for digital power conversion application. Test results are obtained by conducting experiment on the PSFB converter of TIDM-02009 reference design.

articleTitle: Multi-switch Fault Diagnosis for the Voltage Source Inverter fed Multi-phase Motor Drives Based on Machine Learning
abstract: Existing fault diagnosis methods cannot be used to various types of multi-phase machines due to different types of stator phase arrangements and its faults. With the advent of big data and artificial intelligence, a machine-learning-based fault diagnosis approach is proposed for multi-phase drive for an electric transportation applications. In this paper, the possible ML techniques and their performance have been studied and implemented for the five-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) fed induction motor drive. For this, the possible switch faults (open and short) has been considered to collect the data for training and testing. The testing comparative results have been presented for fault detection and classification.

articleTitle: PWM Inverter Based Active Filter for High Frequency AC Systems in Space Applications
abstract: This article describes a PWM inverter based shunt active filtering scheme for high frequency AC systems in space applications. A relatively simple control architecture using only proportional, integral, and resonant controllers along with a sec-ond order generalised integrator is proposed for the shunt filter.
