The controllers are designed such that they are implementable using Op-Amp based analog circuits which is preferable for space application. Example design parameters are given for designing the analog controllers. Simulation results are shown to compare the performance of the proposed system with classical passive filter based compensation. Dynamic response of the proposed system due to load change is also shown.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable DC-Link Capacitor based AC- DC Converter with Multi - Function Controller for Versatile Loads
abstract: This paper proposes an AC-DC converter with a reconfigurable DC-Link capacitor. In the reconfigurable DC-Link, the electrolytic capacitor is connected and disconnected by the operating relay/contactor. When the DC-Link capacitor is connected, the converter functions as a two-stage system consisting of AC-DC and DC-DC converter. When the DC-Link capacitor is disconnected, the converter operates as a single-stage AC- DC converter. Additionally, within the two-stage system, two control strategies have been discussed, one involving a variable DC link voltage and the other with a fixed DC link voltage. Overall, the proposed converter can operate using three control strategies and can supply power to versatile loads, leveraging the advantages of these strategies across both stages. The operation and control of the proposed converter have been discussed, followed by the experimental results obtained from a scaled-down prototype implemented using TMS320F28335.

articleTitle: Generalized Analytical Modeling for Switching Loss Estimation of SiC MOSFET at Wide Operating Range
abstract: In the present era, the most significant goal for any power engineer is to enhance the system efficiency while operating at higher switching frequency and high power ratings. Wide band gap devices (such as SiC and GaN) plays crucial role in reduction of semiconductor losses and enhancement in power handling capability of power converter. However, precise estimation of switching and conduction losses in semiconductor devices is critical and challenging. The conventional techniques for loss calculation involves double pulse test (DPT) and calorimetric test (CT) provides good accuracy but it requires a dedicated test setup. Implementing a test environment for loss estimation is a practically insignificant and unfeasible option. This paper proposes a generalized algorithm for developing a simple analytical loss estimation model by using device datasheet information. The proposed model has capability to accurately and quickly estimate switching losses for wider range of operating voltage and current. This article also explains an excellent strategy for extracting parameters from datasheets by curve fitting. To verify the proposed model, DPT is performed on SiC based half bridge inverter.

articleTitle: A Long Horizon Data Augmentation Technique to Produce Reliable Synthetic Battery Parameters
abstract: Battery driven Electric Vehicles have created huge inroads into the conventional transportation sector over the past decade. Lowered cost and greater energy density numbers have encouraged many gasoline powered automakers to explore electrifying their future fleet of vehicles. State-of-Charge algo-rithm validation and inference has amassed a lot of commer-cial and research interest from the energy storage community. State-of-Charge essentially indicates the remaining range of the vehicle. Data driven techniques have enabled researchers to design accurate State-of-Charge computation algorithms but finite and restricted data availability is worrisome. This paper introduces a competent data augmentation technique which will help to generate error-free synthetic data. We show that such an approach greatly diminishes the limited data challenge. We release the code implementation of our work in the results section to allow reliable reproduction of our work by all battery data scientists. Code and data can be found at this URL: https://github.com/vageeshmaiya/Temporal-Fusion-Transformer

articleTitle: Challenges Posed by Renewable Energy Source Integration to Machine Learning Based Power System Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Nowadays machine learning (ML)-based power system fault diagnosis is being researched to a great extent. ML techniques have many advantages over conventional fault diagnosis techniques. However, with the advent of renewable energy sources (RES) integration on a large scale it is necessary to study whether ML models will be able to adapt to new RES integration. In this paper, a performance investigation of a few ML techniques has been done for power system fault classification and localization on new solar PV plant integration to the IEEE 9 Bus system. The proposed performance investigation is an impact analysis of new RES integration on ML model performance when fault data for RES integrated system is unavailable. Thus, fault classification and localization of RES integrated power system faults are predicted from pre-trained ML models, that were trained from conventional power system fault data. The results revealed that ML models' performance degrades severely with RES integration.

articleTitle: A Dual Input Bipolar Symmetrical Output DC-DC Converter with Improved Voltage Gain
abstract: The article explores a novel multi-port converter specifically designed for interfacing Solar PV and battery systems to bipolar load setups, consolidating power transfer within a single stage. The proposed converter demonstrates an improved voltage gain compared to contemporary non-isolated multi-input DC-DC converters, while exhibiting more lenient port voltage constraints, thereby enhancing the system's overall operational flexibility. Capable of executing as a single-input-triple-output, dual-input-dual-output, or single-input-dual-output system, the introduced converter adapts to the dynamic energy interactions between the source and the load. Furthermore, the converter achieves current control for the PV source and inherently balances both pole voltages using a simplified control strategy due to its consistent dynamic model. The article delves into various operational modes and presents steady-state and dynamic simulation results, highlighting the efficacy of the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: Active Flux-based Torque Compensation Method of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors for Traction Application
abstract: This technical paper presents an approach for torque estimation in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) through Active flux estimation employing model reference adaptive observer (MRAO). The proposed method demonstrates applicability across diverse PMSM motor types, including Interior Permanent Magnet (IPM), Surface Permanent Magnet (SPM), and Synchronous Reluctance Motors (SynRM). Leveraging Popov's hyperstability criterion for parameter adaptation enhances the robustness and accuracy of torque estimation, addressing challenges associated with varying operating conditions. Furthermore, the paper introduces a torque compensation mechanism based on the estimated torque values. This feature contributes to the overall control system's efficiency by mitigating torque discrepancies and ensuring precise motor performance throughout its operating conditions. Simulations with high fidelity FEA data of motor and experimental verifications on four different motor prototypes further support the usability of the proposed method especially for traction application.

articleTitle: Reliability Consequence of using Optimal Gbit Flash Memory based PWM Inverters
abstract: The Gbit-size Flash Memory based Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) algorithms for three-phase inverters differ from the conventional counter-based implementation since they follow a pre-programmed optimal PWM pattern. At a fixed sampling interval, each position within the complex plane may correspond to a different sequence of states or pulse structure. The simultaneous optimization of harmonics and power loss was demonstrated with Gbit-size Flash Memory based Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) algorithms. This allows for lifetime and reliability improvement. This paper offers lifetime and reliability calculation for the Gbit-size Flash Memory based Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) algorithms showing their advantage brought with reduction of thermal stress.

articleTitle: Design to Improve Performance in Two-Stage 48-to-1V Architecture for Server Power Supply
abstract: The voltage regulator modules (VRMs) designed for the 48 V bus architecture necessitate high efficiency and compactness, along with fast dynamic performance across a wide range of input voltage and load conditions. This paper investigates modern architectures suitable for these high conversion factor converters, categorizing them into three groups based on their fundamental power processing principles. A comparative analysis is conducted among these categories, and based on a) simplicity in design, b) adherence to regulation criteria, c) non-isolated structure, and d) flat efficiency profile throughout the load range, the cascaded architecture is selected. A cascaded two-stage converter is proposed, featuring a 4:1 Active Half-Bridge converter for the first stage to step down the nominal 48 V input to an intermediate 12 V bus voltage for the last stage converter. The last stage employs a buck-derived series capacitor buck converter, leveraging reduced device stress and digital current mode control. Simulation studies demonstrate the fast dynamic response of both stage converters under a 60 W step load change. An initial hardware prototype is constructed, and experimental results validate the design's efficacy for a 60 A step load change with a 48 V input voltage and 1 V output voltage.

articleTitle: An Improved Fundamental Current Estimation Algorithm for Traction Drives in Overmodulation Zone
abstract: Squirrel Cage Induction Motors (SCIM) are widely used in traction applications. Traction drives are usually op-erated in the overmodulation zone to enhance the utilization of the DC bus voltage. However, the inverter output voltage contains a lower-order harmonic voltages in the overmodulation zone. These harmonic voltages result in lower-order harmonic currents in SCIM, which can deteriorate the performance of the closed-loop drive. Therefore, a suitable fundamental current estimation algorithm is required. The correct motor parameters are necessary to estimate precise fundamental current, which is sometimes difficult to estimate. This article proposes an improved fundamental current estimation algorithm, which estimates the leakage inductance error and updates it in real time. The proposed algorithm is simulated and verified in SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Dual Output Five-Level Converter with Reduced Switch Count
abstract: This work presents a novel dual output five-level voltage (FL- DOV) converter topology designed to supply two independent loads simultaneously. The proposed FL-DOV converter significantly reduces the number of switches required compared to traditional five-level multilevel inverters (MLIs) when driving two loads. This reduction in switch count leads to decreased complexity and potential cost savings. A level-shifted in-phase disposition pulse width modulation (PWM) technique is utilized to achieve efficient switching and improved performance. Extensive simulation studies conducted in the MATLAB/Simulink environment demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed converter. The results validate the FL-DOV converter's capability to deliver efficient and reliable power to two loads concurrently. This research advances the dual-output inverters by presenting a more efficient and streamlined solution for powering two loads, contributing to the development of versatile and cost-effective power electronic systems.

articleTitle: Non-Isolated Partial Power Processing Converter for Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: This paper presents a Partial Power Processing (PPP) type bidirectional converter for interfacing Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with a DC grid. A non-isolated Series-Pass Partial Power Processing converter is conceptualized, and a Four-Switch Buck-Boost (FSBB) converter is used to realize the power stage. The steady-state analysis of the proposed topology is discussed. A circuit simulation model for the proposed converter is developed, and its operation is validated for different operating modes. A laboratory prototype of the FSBB converter has been developed, and experimental results are presented to validate the functionality of the proposed topology. It is demonstrated that the FSBB converter, rated at 40 % of the total power, facilitates power transfer up to 800 W between the source and the load with a system efficiency close to 94 %.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of a GaN-based high-efficiency Dual Active Bridge Converter
abstract: Dual active bridge (DAB) based DC-DC converters are attractive choices over LLC-based resonant converters for EV charging applications due to their constant frequency operation and full bidirectional power flow capability. GaN HEMTs are available commercially in the voltage range of 650V and it superior to state-of-the-art Si Super-junction MOSFET (Si SJMOS) due to their better conduction and switching performances. In this context, the paper provides an optimal design approach for GaN HEMT-based high-frequency DAB converter for EV charging applications. Single phase shift (SPS) modulation along with frequency variation is used to achieve wider zero voltage switching (ZVS) range. The specification of the converter assumes the input voltage is fixed to 400V and the output voltage varies in the range of 200-460V. The maximum output power is 6.6kW and the frequency is varied in the range of 400kHz to 600kHz. A hardware prototype is implemented to validate the design with 650V, 60A GaN HEMT. The designed converter can operate over a wide range of output voltage while maintaining the ZVS.

articleTitle: Quasi- Two-Level Switching for Active Balancing of Flying Capacitor Multilevel Converters Under Light-Load Conditions
abstract: This work presents a quasi-two-Ievel (Q2L) switching scheme and accompanying controller for active balancing of capacitor voltages in the Flying Capacitor Multilevel Converter. Compared to prior work relying on Phase-Shifted Pulse-Width Modulation, the proposed switching scheme enables active balancing at average load currents approaching and equal to zero. The proposed switching method and active balancing controller are validated in a 6-level hardware prototype, verifying capacitor voltage tracking at light-load under supply voltage transients.

articleTitle: A Nonisolated Four-Port DC-DC Converter for Solar PV-Battery Integration in Bipolar Load Systems
abstract: The article introduces a new four-port converter formulated for integration of Solar PV and battery into bipolar DC microgrid systems, achieving single-stage energy conversion. Distinguished by its improved power density, incorporating single inductor, the proposed circuit exhibits enhanced voltage boost in contrast to contemporary non-isolated multiport DC-DC converters. Notably, all input and output ports share a common reference ground. The symmetrical structure at the output inherently regulates both pole voltages, while ensuring inductor current control leveraging a simplified control strategy. Moreover, the proposed converter is capable of executing as a single-input-triple-output, dual-input-dual-output, or single-input-dual-output system based on the energy relationships between the source and the load. The article explores various operational modes and presents simulation results highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: Universal Modulation Technique for Quasi-Hybrid Input based Dual-Active-Bridge Converter for Bidirectional V2G Applications
abstract: This paper introduces a universal modulation technique (UMT) for the bidirectional dual-active-bridge (DAB) converter that is supplied by a quasi-hybrid input (AC or DC). The presented UMT is versatile, adaptable, working smoothly with any inputs, and capable of supplying or drawing power for AC or DC grid. Out of eight high-frequency switches of DAB, the presented modulation eliminates turn-ON loss for all switches and turn-OFF loss for six switches. It is easy to realize due to the single control variable, offering power factor correction (PFC) during grid-to-vehicle (G2V). To realize this modulation technique, a quasi-single-stage (QS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) bidirectional DAB is selected which can operate in AC-to-DC or DC-to-DC mode. Further, to implement the UMT, two configurations for the QS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> DAB are presented: one features a single port serving both AC and DC inputs, while the other includes two separate ports with power relay. For quasi-hybrid input, a control scheme applicable to both configurations with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and G2V features is discussed. Additionally, design criteria are presented considering the real-world rating. The proposed idea has been tested and verified using a scaled-down prototype of 630 W.

articleTitle: Open Circuit Fault-Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Operation of ANPC
abstract: This paper introduces a real-time fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant method for detecting open-circuit (OC) faults in insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) for a three-phase active neutral point clamp (3L-ANPC) converter. The strategy utilizes pole voltage as an input, and based on the deviation between the output pole voltage and the applied switching state, identifies any faulty switches. This approach is load-independent and does not require additional current information. Practical implementation of the strategy only necessitates three additional pole voltage sensors. This diagnostic method enables faster fault detection, typically within one switching cycle under favourable conditions, and can also detect multiple OC failures using the same strategy. Experimental and simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Phase Quadruple Boost Switched Capacitor Multilevel Inverter for PV Applications
abstract: Switched-capacitor based multilevel inverter (SC-ML) topologies are gaining attention due to their self-voltage balancing and boosting capabilities. It requires lesser values of DC-link voltage to achieve the desired magnitude of output voltage. Therefore, SC-ML converters significantly contribute for the application of renewable sources especially with solar photovoltaic (PV). Hence, this paper proposed a new three-phase quadruple boost multi-level inverter (QBMLI) topology with switched capacitors for PV applications. The proposed QBMLI generates nine-levels by utilizing two switched capacitors, fewer power electronic switches, and diodes. A level shifted multi-carrier pulse width modulation (PWM) is employed to enhance the quality of output voltage consisting of lower harmonics and high RMS voltages. The proposed topology initially developed in MATLAB/Simulink environment and the per-formance is observed by considering various indices such as modulation index and switching frequency. Furthermore, the system performance is validated in real-time using dSPACE Scalexio based Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL).

articleTitle: Effectiveness Study of Streamlined Fin with Low-Pressure Loss to Improve Heat Dissipation Performance of Heat Sink
abstract: In recent years, with the advent of next-generation semiconductors, circuit boards have been miniaturized to accommodate higher frequencies. Miniaturization also means increased heat density. Further miniaturization of switching converters and inverters requires heat sinks that provide excellent heat dissipation performance in a limited volume, and the cylindrical fin type has been commonly used as a heat sink structure. However, cylindrical fin type heat sinks have the problem of large pressure loss when refrigerant passes through them. To solve this problem, streamlined fins and elliptical fin have been proposed to replace cylindrical fin type heat sinks. Although many studies have compared the heat dissipation performance of elliptical and cylindrical fin, few studies have compared it with that of streamlined fins. Therefore, in this paper, a heat sink structure with multiple streamlined fins is constructed. The change in pressure loss due to the change in fin shape and the resulting heat dissipation performance were verified by thermo-fluid analysis and actual device verification, and compared with the conventional cylindrical fin type. As a result, it was confirmed that the streamlined fin structure slightly increases thermal resistance and significantly reduces pressure loss. Comparison of the thermal resistance-pressure loss characteristics showed that the streamlined fins can sufficiently reduce the pressure loss for the same thermal resistance value. In the case of forced air cooling, the heat dissipation performance of the streamlined fins could be expected to improve with fan selection.

articleTitle: Comparison of Availability and Resiliency Planning for Critical Loads
abstract: This paper discusses fundamental notions for planning resilient and reliable powering of critical loads, such as information and communications technology (ICT) sites, and compares strategies for such purpose. In particular, this paper explains the fundamental differences between higher availability and higher resilience planning beyond the basic common notion that the former applies to normal operating condition and the latter for uncommon extreme events. Implications of these differences are also explored. Additionally, this paper explores how to take into consideration adaptation and planning activities for higher availability or higher resilience. In order to support this discussion this paper makes use of a model representing the effects of gensets refueling processes on availability and resilience. Uncertainty costs involved in these planning processes are, then, explored. Relationships between reliability and resilience planning are also discussed.

articleTitle: Control of Cascaded H - Bridge and Series Resonant Dual Active Bridge (DC-DC) based Solid State Transformer under Unbalance Grid
abstract: Due to the recent developments in power electronics, Solid State Transformer (SST) technology is now the preeminent solution for smart grid systems in generation and distribution networks. However unbalanced grid voltage conditions in the MVAC/LVAC grid can significantly degrade the power quality of SST. Due to the existence of negative components arising due to unbalance voltage in the grid, it produces oscillations in active and reactive power. Hence it is vital to design a control architecture to operate the SST proficiently under an unbalanced grid. This article introduces a control architecture to control positive and negative sequence currents in the LV and MV stages of SST independently. In the proposed technique, a current reference generation algorithm is introduced to suppress active power ripples at the MV/LV stage converter terminals. The proposed control architecture is validated in MATLAB Simulink on a 1.65 kV (MV)/500V(LVDC)/300V(LV), CHB-based SST.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Dynamic Mho Characteristic to PLL Parameters of Grid Following PV
abstract: The restructuring of the power system by replacing Synchronous Generators (SGs) with Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) has resulted in a drastic change in power system dynamics. Positive Sequence Memory Polarized (PSMP) mho elements have been used to ensure the reliable operation of mho relays during close-in bolted faults. The use of memory voltage for polarization of the mho element causes dynamic expansion of the mho characteristics. In an SG-only system, the memory polarization-induced dynamic expansion of these mho characteristics helps to increase the resistive reach. However, as the integration of IBRs increases, the dynamic mho expansion will be affected due to the different fault characteristics of IBRs. Most IBRs currently integrated into the power system are Grid-Following (GFOL) type, which uses Phase-Locked Loops (PLL) for synchronization. The variations in control parameters and bandwidths of the PLLs used in the GFOL IBRs may also affect the dynamic mho expansion. The studies presented in this paper demonstrate the impact of different types of PLLs and their control parameters on the dynamic expansion of PSMP mho relays. For this analysis, a modified IEEE-39 bus system with a GFOL Photovoltaic (PV) generator is used. The PV s have Voltage Support (VS), Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT)/ High Voltage Ride-Through (HVRT) features and comply with IEEE 2800–2022 standard.

articleTitle: Microgrids for Base Stations: Increased Cellular Network Resiliency through Integration of Solar Energy and Virtual Energy Transfer
abstract: Batteries banks or photovoltaic (PV) arrays can increase cellular cell sites resiliency to disruptions in the electricity supply from the local utility, but their deployment is challenging in small cell sites due to size limitations on the power backup components. This work presents a novel approach to leverage PV arrays at large cell sites, where small cells increase their resiliency by receiving a virtual energy transfer (VET) from a macro cell that is equipped with a PV array. Also, this work is the first to evaluate the performance of VET under dynamic load conditions. The results show that VET provides useful increases in resiliency for small cells, yielding an energy buffer autonomy increase of at least 14% (in the least favorable setup), while even a modest-size PV array allows the macro BS to provide VET without any sacrifice in its resiliency.

articleTitle: Design Comparison and Investigations into Thermal Failure of HF Transformers in Isolated DC-DC Converters
abstract: Ferrite transformer magnetics in high-frequency ap-plication space are traditionally designed to meet the desired power-handling capability through a selection process cognizant of core saturation limits and conductor ampacity, while being aware of the power loss incurred. While the electro-magnetic behavior of the device is typically treated as the key performance thrust for design verification, the thermal characteristics of the structure, especially from a dynamic standpoint and its impact on the operational performance, are seldom investigated. Recognizing this, the paper focuses on the thermal behavior of a ferrite core-based high-frequency (HF) transformer using a phase-shifted full-bridge (PSFB) converter as a use case. First, we examine two widely popular methodologies leveraged in literature for HF-transformer sizing and selection and share perspectives on their outcomes against the backdrop considered here. Next, we experimentally report a thermal failure mode that is induced by the dynamics of temperature rise rather than the quantum of temperature rise itself, which is typically unanticipated and never accounted for in the upfront design considerations. We present pertinent theoretical perspectives on the same, furnish 3D FEA simulation outcomes in ANSYS, and provide experimental results from a 1.5kW hardware setup.

articleTitle: Program Booklet Intelec24
1 MHz Isolation Transformer Design, Using the Core Geometry Approach
abstract: In this paper, the design of a 1 MHz isolation transformer using a core geometry optimization approach is presented. The transformer is designed with a unity turn ratio, making it ideal for isolation transformers in dual active bridge DC-DC converters. Key parameters, including input power, frequency, regulation, maximum duty cycle, window utilization, operating flux density, waveform factor, minimum input voltage, and efficiency, are optimized. The optimization process involves the random generation of these parameters within specified ranges, followed by detailed design calculations to minimize total loss and maximize power density and efficiency. The method utilizes MATLAB and Python for modeling and Monte Carlo simulations, ensuring a comprehensive analysis of the transformer performance. The designed transformer has been tested with simulations and experimental results on a 250W model, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed method. Detailed design considerations, numerical values, and experimental results are included, demonstrating significant improvements in transformer performance. This method provides valuable insights for the design of high-frequency isolation transformers, contributing to the advancement of efficient and reliable systems. The comprehensive approach and thorough validation underscore the practical applicability and robustness of the proposed design optimization technique.
